scoring_justification: Recomputing formation energies from raw DFT total energies is infeasible in the checker sandbox; therefore we verify structural properties: relative ordering (Fe5_Ti2 > Fe3_VO_U2) and correct sign (isolated defect positive, complex negative).

hidden_assets.purpose: Define structural checks based on paper's results: isolated Fe5+ at Ti(2) has positive formation energy (0.226 eV), Fe3+-VO U2 complex has negative formation energy (-1.6774 eV). These structural rules are derived from the paper's Tables I and II.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table I: Fe5+ at Ti(2) formation energy 0.226 eV; Table II: Fe3+-VO U2 formation energy -1.6774 eV.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own reported values, used only to define the structural sign checks; the checker does not compare against exact values, only checks ordering and sign.

outputs.description: Formation energies of two defect configurations: Fe⁵⁺ at Ti(2) site (electronically compensated) and Fe³⁺–V_O at U2 configuration (vacancy compensated) evaluated under air conditions.

output_contract.notes: The checker verifies that Fe5_Ti2 > Fe3_VO_U2 and both values lie in a physically plausible range.

steps.description: Verify ordering (Fe5_Ti2 > Fe3_VO_U2) and correct sign (Fe5_Ti2 > 0, Fe3_VO_U2 < 0) to reflect the paper's conclusion that isolated defects have positive formation energies while the complex is negative.
